title: One Day, $1,000 in Tokens: An AI War Room for Legacy Code — Ford Prior, GEICO
talk_summary: GEICO ran a one-day, ~$1,000-token 'war room' where a markdown-defined fleet manager (FleetKit) decomposed a legacy-modernization goal, dispatched research/leader agents, gated decisions through human-approvable artifacts (worksheets, design docs), then dispatched builder agents to produce a deployable change. They repeated it across three domains and found cheaper models matched expensive ones on benchmarks.

takeaways.technique: Markdown-defined fleet manager with leader/builder split
takeaways.what_they_do: A rules/protocols markdown layer above system prompts takes a goal, breaks it down, dispatches leader agents to research and decide approach, queues decisions for human approval, then dispatches builder agents to implement.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Takes a goal, breaks it down, dispatches leaders to do all the research, and decide about the approach... when everything looks tight from a approval standpoint, it dispatches builders

takeaways.what_they_do: Each milestone produces a fillable artifact (HTML worksheet or design doc) that humans edit and the agent re-reads; heavy human input early, tapering off as the run proceeds.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it creates these worksheets that are like actually really well-done HTML... People can fill them out. They're automatically saved... to fill the gaps

takeaways.technique: Benchmark cheaper model against golden data before defaulting to expensive
takeaways.what_they_do: After building context, they benchmarked a cheaper model against recently-written real code as golden data and found it matched or beat the expensive model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we ran benchmarks... using our existing code recently written as the golden data and found out that Fable or uh Sonnet 5.5 wrote it just as good as if not better than Fable

takeaways.what_they_do: They found agents scheduling crons to check on work spawned a fresh expensive session each tick and burned budget.
takeaways.evidence_quote: do not let uh Claude running Fable set up crons to check on work uh because you'll it'll just launch a Claude uh a Fable session each time and burn your budget immediately

takeaways.what_they_do: The code-modernization plugin deterministically verifies the previous step produced its required artifacts (including a file) before proceeding.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it does like a deterministic analysis of like did the previous step create the artifacts that it needed to, including a file

takeaways.technique: Plain-markdown context repos, agent- and human-editable
takeaways.what_they_do: All domain context, standards, methods, and judgment rules live in two plain markdown repos that both agents and humans can add to and correct.
takeaways.evidence_quote: our context was just like markdown files, y'all. Like we didn't really have any complex way to graph things out
